correctness.independent_verification: Independently evaluated degree 1–8 polynomial intensity DFTs on two radii (nonaligned offsets) and recovered a_d conjugate(a_0) from the explicit 2×2 Nyquist equations in all eight constructed cases. Source script verify_two_circle_nyquist.py was read fully; general statement follows exact Fourier/reflection proof, not the eight numerical cases.
correctness.rationale: For f(z)=Σ_{0≤m≤d}a_m z^m, each circle intensity has harmonics from −d to d. Sampling at N=2d regular polygon phases recovers c_m(r) for |m|<d exactly, and only the ±d Nyquist collision remains. Because c_d(r)=r^d a_d conjugate(a_0), the two alternating real samples recover its two real coordinates iff the 2×2 angular matrix determinant −sin[d(θ2−θ1)] is nonzero. This yields full continuous moduli on both distinct circles; applying rational-function Schwarz reflection for each radius and dilation invariance R(z)=R((r2/r1)² z) forces f/g to be a unimodular constant, including zero and vanishing coefficients. At aligned phases z^d±i e^{idθ1} are indistinguishable. The de-aliasing Gram eigenvalues 1±|cos[d(θ2−θ1)]| give the exact normalized subsystem condition number and unique halfstep optimum. This does NOT claim global nonlinear inverse stability or minimality beyond this regular balanced geometry.

value.rationale: Two concentric regular intensity polygons with exactly equal sample allocations are a natural constrained experimental geometry. The theorem gives both a complete yes/no design classification and the exact angular staggering that optimizes the only nontrivial linear de-aliasing subsystem. The aligned-grid ambiguity gives a motivated sharp boundary; full nonlinear stability is not asserted. Thus it is more than routine interpolation or a numerical experiment.
